Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. `dmtools <alias> --help` (and `dmtools list <alias>`) now resolve the filter through `ToolRegistry.resolveToolAlias` before the substring filter, so aliased tools print the resolved backend tool's schema instead of `{"tools": []}`.

### Key decisions

# gh-136: CLI: tool help/list mode does not resolve aliases — tracker_get_ticket --help prints {"tools":[]}

## Description

## Bug
Direct tool invocation help is broken for aliased tools:

```
$ dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help
{
  "tools": []
}
```

Expected: the tool's usage/schema (same output shape as for a canonical tool, e.g. `dmtools github_get_issue --help`).

## Root cause hypothesis
The `--help` path in the CLI dispatcher falls into the tool-list/filter mode, and the list filter does NOT go through `resolveToolAlias` (cli_dispatcher.dart, Java parity: `McpCliHandler.resolveToolAlias`). So `tracker_*` aliases (and any alias names) match nothing → empty list. Canonical names presumably work — verify.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)
- [ ] same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)
- [ ] canonical `--help` unchanged
- [ ] unit tests: alias resolution in the help/list path (cli_dispatcher tests)

## Notes
- Java spec: dm.ai `McpCliHandler` — help resolution mirrors invocation resolution.
- Found via the machine-loop E2E (sm_github.json rule pack dogfooding).

Now let me understand the behavior. `_listTools` now resolves the alias and falls back to substring filter with the raw text if unresolved.

Key considerations:

1. `resolveToolAlias` returns the first candidate when an alias has multiple carriers and no default is set. So `tracker_get_ticket --help` with DEFAULT_TRACKER unset → resolves to `jira_get_ticket`. Then `filterToolsList(response, 'jira_get_ticket')` — substring filter matches `jira_get_ticket` exactly. OK.

2. But wait — a subtle behavior change: For a canonical tool name with an *empty* candidate list — `resolveToolAlias` returns `null` for unknown names → fall back to raw substring. OK.

3. What about the behavior of `dmtools list <canonical substring>`? E.g., `dmtools list jira` — `resolveToolAlias('jira')` → `_tools.containsKey('jira')` false, candidates empty → null → falls back to `jira` substring. Unchanged. Good.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks
  the agents' `postPRReviewComments` `pr_approved` hand-off on `gh-N`
  tickets.
- TestRail section-aware case creation, porting Java PR
  [epam/dm.ai#462](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/462):
  `testrail_get_sections` (`project_name` + optional `suite_id`, paginated,
  always fetched fresh) and the `testrail_create_case`,
  `testrail_create_case_detailed`, `testrail_create_case_steps` tools with an
  optional `section_id` that falls back to the project's default section
  (creating a "Test Cases" section when the project has none). Markdown
  tables in text fields convert to TestRail `|||:Col|Col` format or HTML for
===

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - **Updated**: 2026-09-16T21:42:14Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`dmtools <alias> --help` (and `dmtools list <alias>`) now resolve the filter through `ToolRegistry.resolveToolAlias` before the substring filter, so aliased tools print the resolved backend tool's schema instead of `{"tools": []}`.

### Key decisions
- Fix lives in `CliDispatcher._listTools` — the shared help/list filter path named as root cause in gh-136; help resolution now mirrors invocation resolution (Java `McpCliHandler` contract).
- Alias defaults (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` / `DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODE`) resolve through the same property chain as invocation, so `dmtools.env` routing works for help too.
- Unresolved filter text (partial names, free text) keeps raw substring semantics — `dmtools list jira` is unchanged.
- Note: `source_code_get_commit_info` (named in the ticket) does not exist in this port's registry nor upstream Java; the `source_code_*` family is covered via `source_code_get_pr`.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/cli_dispatcher_alias_test.dart
dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help                 # jira_get_ticket schema (DEFAULT_TRACKER unset)
DEFAULT_TRACKER=github dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help   # github_get_issue schema
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help"] --> D["CliDispatcher._toolDispatch"]
  D -->|help flag| L["_listTools"]
  L --> R["resolveToolAlias + DEFAULT_TRACKER/SOURCE_CODE"]
  R --> F["filterToolsList (resolved name)"]
  F --> O["backend tool schema JSON"]
```

</details>

# gh-136: CLI: tool help/list mode does not resolve aliases — tracker_get_ticket --help prints {"tools":[]}

## Description

## Bug
Direct tool invocation help is broken for aliased tools:

```
$ dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help
{
  "tools": []
}
```

Expected: the tool's usage/schema (same output shape as for a canonical tool, e.g. `dmtools github_get_issue --help`).

## Root cause hypothesis
The `--help` path in the CLI dispatcher falls into the tool-list/filter mode, and the list filter does NOT go through `resolveToolAlias` (cli_dispatcher.dart, Java parity: `McpCliHandler.resolveToolAlias`). So `tracker_*` aliases (and any alias names) match nothing → empty list. Canonical names presumably work — verify.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)
- [ ] same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)
- [ ] canonical `--help` unchanged
- [ ] unit tests: alias resolution in the help/list path (cli_dispatcher tests)

## Notes
- Java spec: dm.ai `McpCliHandler` — help resolution mirrors invocation resolution.
- Found via the machine-loop E2E (sm_github.json rule pack dogfooding).

Aliases don't appear in the tools list JSON anyway (tools are keyed by canonical name; aliases aren't in the JSON output... let me check `toJson` of ToolDefinition). # AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks
  the agents' `postPRReviewComments` `pr_approved` hand-off on `gh-N`
  tickets.
- TestRail section-aware case creation, porting Java PR
  [epam/dm.ai#462](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/462):
  `testrail_get_sections` (`project_name` + optional `suite_id`, paginated,
  always fetched fresh) and the `testrail_create_case`,
  `testrail_create_case_detailed`, `testrail_create_case_steps` tools with an
  optional `section_id` that falls back to the project's default section
  (creating a "Test Cases" section when the project has none). Markdown
  tables in text fields convert to TestRail `|||:Col|Col` format or HTML for
===

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

### What changed
`dmtools <alias> --help` (and `dmtools list <alias>`) now resolve the filter through `ToolRegistry.resolveToolAlias` before the substring filter, so aliased tools print the resolved backend tool's schema instead of `{"tools": []}`.

### Key decisions

- Alias defaults (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` / `DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODE`) resolve through the same property chain as invocation, so `dmtools.env` routing works for help too.

# gh-136: CLI: tool help/list mode does not resolve aliases — tracker_get_ticket --help prints {"tools":[]}

## Description

## Bug
Direct tool invocation help is broken for aliased tools:

```
$ dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help
{
  "tools": []
}
```

Expected: the tool's usage/schema (same output shape as for a canonical tool, e.g. `dmtools github_get_issue --help`).

## Root cause hypothesis
The `--help` path in the CLI dispatcher falls into the tool-list/filter mode, and the list filter does NOT go through `resolveToolAlias` (cli_dispatcher.dart, Java parity: `McpCliHandler.resolveToolAlias`). So `tracker_*` aliases (and any alias names) match nothing → empty list. Canonical names presumably work — verify.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)
- [ ] same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)
- [ ] canonical `--help` unchanged
- [ ] unit tests: alias resolution in the help/list path (cli_dispatcher tests)

## Notes
- Java spec: dm.ai `McpCliHandler` — help resolution mirrors invocation resolution.
- Found via the machine-loop E2E (sm_github.json rule pack dogfooding).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other

## PR Description

### What changed
`dmtools <alias> --help` (and `dmtools list <alias>`) now resolve the filter through `ToolRegistry.resolveToolAlias` before the substring filter, so aliased tools print the resolved backend tool's schema instead of `{"tools": []}`.

### Key decisions
- Fix lives in `CliDispatcher._listTools` — the shared help/list filter path named as root cause in gh-136; help resolution now mirrors invocation resolution (Java `McpCliHandler` contract).
- Alias defaults (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` / `DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODE`) resolve through the same property chain as invocation, so `dmtools.env` routing works for help too.
- Unresolved filter text (partial names, free text) keeps raw substring semantics — `dmtools list jira` is unchanged.
- Note: `source_code_get_commit_info` (named in the ticket) does not exist in this port's registry nor upstream Java; the `source_code_*` family is covered via `source_code_get_pr`.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/cli_dispatcher_alias_test.dart
dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help                 # jira_get_ticket schema (DEFAULT_TRACKER unset)
DEFAULT_TRACKER=github dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help   # github_get_issue schema
```

# gh-136: CLI: tool help/list mode does not resolve aliases — tracker_get_ticket --help prints {"tools":[]}

## Description

## Bug
Direct tool invocation help is broken for aliased tools:

```
$ dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help
{
  "tools": []
}
```

Expected: the tool's usage/schema (same output shape as for a canonical tool, e.g. `dmtools github_get_issue --help`).

## Root cause hypothesis
The `--help` path in the CLI dispatcher falls into the tool-list/filter mode, and the list filter does NOT go through `resolveToolAlias` (cli_dispatcher.dart, Java parity: `McpCliHandler.resolveToolAlias`). So `tracker_*` aliases (and any alias names) match nothing → empty list. Canonical names presumably work — verify.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)
- [ ] same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)
- [ ] canonical `--help` unchanged
- [ ] unit tests: alias resolution in the help/list path (cli_dispatcher tests)

## Notes
- Java spec: dm.ai `McpCliHandler` — help resolution mirrors invocation resolution.
- Found via the machine-loop E2E (sm_github.json rule pack dogfooding).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks
  the agents' `postPRReviewComments` `pr_approved` hand-off on `gh-N`
  tickets.
- TestRail section-aware case creation, porting Java PR
  [epam/dm.ai#462](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/462):
  `testrail_get_sections` (`project_name` + optional `suite_id`, paginated,
  always fetched fresh) and the `testrail_create_case`,
  `testrail_create_case_detailed`, `testrail_create_case_steps` tools with an
  optional `section_id` that falls back to the project's default section
  (creating a "Test Cases" section when the project has none). Markdown
  tables in text fields convert to TestRail `|||:Col|Col` format or HTML for
===

Now let me re-check the DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS edge case more concretely to be sure it's real:

- `DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS=ado` → `_resolveIntegrations()` = {'ado'} → `generateToolsListResponse({'ado'})` → tools = ado tools only.
- `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` → `_toolDispatch` → `_listTools(['tracker_get_ticket'])` → resolveToolAlias('tracker_get_ticket') → candidates [jira_get_ticket (jira), ado_get_work_item (ado), github_get_issue (github)] in registration order → no DEFAULT_TRACKER → returns 'jira_get_ticket' → filter over ado-only list → no match → `{"tools": []}` — the exact bug from the ticket still reproduces under DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS=ado. Also: what if DEFAULT_TRACKER is set to an integration NOT in DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS? Same empty result. Invocation path ignores DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS entirely (the registry is unfiltered), so help vs invocation diverge.

Suggested fix: filter candidates to those present in the generated response, e.g., resolve against `integrations`:
```dart
final resolved = registry.resolveToolAlias(rest.first, ...);
final filter = (resolved != null && responseContains(response, resolved)) ? resolved : rest.first;
```
Better: pass integrations into resolution so the first-candidate fallback picks a visible carrier. I'll describe in the comment.

## PR Description

### What changed
`dmtools <alias> --help` (and `dmtools list <alias>`) now resolve the filter through `ToolRegistry.resolveToolAlias` before the substring filter, so aliased tools print the resolved backend tool's schema instead of `{"tools": []}`.

### Key decisions

# gh-136: CLI: tool help/list mode does not resolve aliases — tracker_get_ticket --help prints {"tools":[]}

## Description

## Bug
Direct tool invocation help is broken for aliased tools:

```
$ dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help
{
  "tools": []
}
```

Expected: the tool's usage/schema (same output shape as for a canonical tool, e.g. `dmtools github_get_issue --help`).

## Root cause hypothesis
The `--help` path in the CLI dispatcher falls into the tool-list/filter mode, and the list filter does NOT go through `resolveToolAlias` (cli_dispatcher.dart, Java parity: `McpCliHandler.resolveToolAlias`). So `tracker_*` aliases (and any alias names) match nothing → empty list. Canonical names presumably work — verify.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)
- [ ] same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)
- [ ] canonical `--help` unchanged
- [ ] unit tests: alias resolution in the help/list path (cli_dispatcher tests)

## Notes
- Java spec: dm.ai `McpCliHandler` — help resolution mirrors invocation resolution.
- Found via the machine-loop E2E (sm_github.json rule pack dogfooding).

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Additions**: +97
- **Deletions**: -1

- **Updated**: 2026-09-16T21:42:14Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`dmtools <alias> --help` (and `dmtools list <alias>`) now resolve the filter through `ToolRegistry.resolveToolAlias` before the substring filter, so aliased tools print the resolved backend tool's schema instead of `{"tools": []}`.

### Key decisions
- Fix lives in `CliDispatcher._listTools` — the shared help/list filter path named as root cause in gh-136; help resolution now mirrors invocation resolution (Java `McpCliHandler` contract).
- Alias defaults (`DEFAULT_TRACKER` / `DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODE`) resolve through the same property chain as invocation, so `dmtools.env` routing works for help too.
- Unresolved filter text (partial names, free text) keeps raw substring semantics — `dmtools list jira` is unchanged.
- Note: `source_code_get_commit_info` (named in the ticket) does not exist in this port's registry nor upstream Java; the `source_code_*` family is covered via `source_code_get_pr`.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/cli_dispatcher_alias_test.dart
dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help                 # jira_get_ticket schema (DEFAULT_TRACKER unset)
DEFAULT_TRACKER=github dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help   # github_get_issue schema
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help"] --> D["CliDispatcher._toolDispatch"]
  D -->|help flag| L["_listTools"]
  L --> R["resolveToolAlias + DEFAULT_TRACKER/SOURCE_CODE"]
  R --> F["filterToolsList (resolved name)"]
  F --> O["backend tool schema JSON"]
```

</details>

# gh-136: CLI: tool help/list mode does not resolve aliases — tracker_get_ticket --help prints {"tools":[]}

## Description

## Bug
Direct tool invocation help is broken for aliased tools:

```
$ dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help
{
  "tools": []
}
```

Expected: the tool's usage/schema (same output shape as for a canonical tool, e.g. `dmtools github_get_issue --help`).

## Root cause hypothesis
The `--help` path in the CLI dispatcher falls into the tool-list/filter mode, and the list filter does NOT go through `resolveToolAlias` (cli_dispatcher.dart, Java parity: `McpCliHandler.resolveToolAlias`). So `tracker_*` aliases (and any alias names) match nothing → empty list. Canonical names presumably work — verify.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)
- [ ] same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)
- [ ] canonical `--help` unchanged
- [ ] unit tests: alias resolution in the help/list path (cli_dispatcher tests)

## Notes
- Java spec: dm.ai `McpCliHandler` — help resolution mirrors invocation resolution.
- Found via the machine-loop E2E (sm_github.json rule pack dogfooding).

Now let me understand the behavior. `_listTools` now resolves the alias and falls back to substring filter with the raw text if unresolved.

Key considerations:

1. `resolveToolAlias` returns the first candidate when an alias has multiple carriers and no default is set. So `tracker_get_ticket --help` with DEFAULT_TRACKER unset → resolves to `jira_get_ticket`. Then `filterToolsList(response, 'jira_get_ticket')` — substring filter matches `jira_get_ticket` exactly. OK.

2. But wait — a subtle behavior change: For a canonical tool name with an *empty* candidate list — `resolveToolAlias` returns `null` for unknown names → fall back to raw substring. OK.

3. What about the behavior of `dmtools list <canonical substring>`? E.g., `dmtools list jira` — `resolveToolAlias('jira')` → `_tools.containsKey('jira')` false, candidates empty → null → falls back to `jira` substring. Unchanged. Good.

4. What about `dmtools list tracker_get_ticket` where the alias has multiple carriers — resolves to the single carrier per default. But what if a user wanted to list all tools matching substring `tracker_get_ticket`? Aliases don't appear in the tools list JSON anyway (tools are keyed by canonical name; aliases aren't in the JSON output... let me check `toJson` of ToolDefinition). Actually filterToolsList filters on name/description only. Alias names wouldn't match anything previously (they aren't tool names). Hmm, but description may contain the alias text? Let me check ToolDefinition.toJson and description content.

5. Edge case: `filterToolsList` matches description substrings too. `resolveToolAlias` could change semantics for a filter text that is *also* an alias but appears in descriptions. E.g., filter "tracker" — not an alias, fine. Filter `source_code_get_pr` — resolves to carrier. But descriptions of other tools might mention `source_code_get_pr`? Unlikely.

But a real behavior change: previously `dmtools list <alias>` returned `{tools: []}` (since alias names don't appear). Now it returns the carrier. That's the intent — improvement.

6. Potential issue: what if `resolveToolAlias` returns a name whose substring is broader? E.g. alias `tracker_get_ticket` resolves to `jira_get_ticket` — filter matches exactly that tool. Fine.

But consider a partial-name filter that *happens* to be an alias... Aliases are full names like `tracker_get_ticket`. Partial names like `jira_search` are not aliases → null → raw. OK.

7. What about `dmtools <tool> --help` where the tool is unknown? Previously `_listTools([toolName])` → filter → empty list `{"tools": []}` exit code 0. Now same — resolveToolAlias returns null → filter with raw → probably empty → `{"tools":[]}` and exit 0. Hmm, that's pre-existing behavior; arguably `dmtools nonexistent_tool --help` printing `{"tools": []}` with exit 0 is suboptimal, but it's not a regression introduced by the PR. The ticket's AC only mentions alias resolution. Could be a SUGGESTION.

8. Test concern: `_dispatchTool(['tracker_search', '--help'], code: 0)` — `filterToolsList(response, 'jira_search_by_jql')` → matches. But note description substring matching: filter `jira_get_ticket` might also match descriptions that contain "jira_get_ticket"? Not relevant.

Wait — one more important check: the test 'dmtools list keeps substring semantics for unknown filters' asserts `names.every((name) => name.startsWith('jira_search'))`. filterToolsList matches name OR description containing the filter. Is there any tool whose description contains 'jira_search' but name doesn't start with jira_search? Presumably not; test passes presumably. Let me run the tests.

9. Multi-carrier resolution and the `--help` output shape: For an alias with multiple carriers and no default, `--help` shows only the first candidate (jira). The PR description acknowledges this. The ticket AC says "prints the resolved backend tool schema (jira_get_ticket or the github backend per DEFAULT_TRACKER)". OK.

10. Ticket AC: "same for other aliases: `tracker_post_comment`, `tracker_search`, `source_code_get_commit_info` (alias family)". PR notes `source_code_get_commit_info` doesn't exist in this port's registry nor upstream Java; covered via `source_code_get_pr`. Let me verify whether `source_code_get_commit_info` exists as alias anywhere. Let me check the default tool registry.

11. DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS interplay: `generateToolsListResponse(integrations)` — if DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS is set to e.g. `ado` but DEFAULT_TRACKER unset, alias resolves to `jira_get_ticket` which is NOT in the response → `{"tools": []}` again! Hmm. Interesting edge case: `DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS=ado dmtools tracker_get_ticket --help` → resolveToolAlias returns jira_get_ticket (first candidate) → filter on a list that only contains ado tools → empty. But note: that's also how *invocation* works? In invocation, `registry.getTool(resolvedTool)` — the ToolRegistry isn't filtered by integrations; the registry contains all tools. So invocation works regardless of DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS. But `_listTools` filters the response by integrations first. So with DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS set to a set not containing the resolved carrier, help still prints `{"tools":[]}`. Is this a realistic concern? In the test environment, `_resolveIntegrations` reads DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS from the reader (test overrides/env cleared). Default is null → all tools. So tests pass. It's an edge case; maybe worth a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT note. Java parity? Unknown. Actually the fix could make resolution happen before the integration filter or check membership. This is a corner case — DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS with aliases. I'd flag as SUGGESTION (edge case).

12. Another subtlety: `_listTools` is also the `list` command handler: `dmtools list tracker_get_ticket` now shows `jira_get_ticket` only, not the other carriers (ado_add_work_item_comment, github_get_issue). If a user wants to see all carriers for an alias... but previously they saw nothing. The PR's semantics choice is documented. OK.

13. Now, is there a case where resolving the filter *narrows* results that previously matched via substring? E.g. filter `source_code_get_pr` is an alias → resolved to carrier e.g. `gitlab_get_mr` → only that tool shown. Previously (before PR), `dmtools list source_code_get_pr` → substring matches tools whose name/description contains `source_code_get_pr` → no tool name contains it... descriptions? Possibly. So previously empty. Now shows carrier. Improvement, no regression.

But wait — what if the resolved name is a *substring* that matches more? resolveToolAlias returns a canonical tool name; filtering by that exact name matches that tool plus any tool whose name/description contains that name as substring. E.g., `github_get_issue` — could match `github_get_issue` and `github_get_issues...`? Minor.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks
  the agents' `postPRReviewComments` `pr_approved` hand-off on `gh-N`
  tickets.
- TestRail section-aware case creation, porting Java PR
  [epam/dm.ai#462](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/462):
  `testrail_get_sections` (`project_name` + optional `suite_id`, paginated,
  always fetched fresh) and the `testrail_create_case`,
  `testrail_create_case_detailed`, `testrail_create_case_steps` tools with an
  optional `section_id` that falls back to the project's default section
  (creating a "Test Cases" section when the project has none). Markdown
  tables in text fields convert to TestRail `|||:Col|Col` format or HTML for
===

Now let me understand the behavior. `_listTools` now resolves the alias and falls back to substring filter with the raw text if unresolved.

Key considerations:

1. `resolveToolAlias` returns the first candidate when an alias has multiple carriers and no default is set. So `tracker_get_ticket --help` with DEFAULT_TRACKER unset → resolves to `jira_get_ticket`. Then `filterToolsList(response, 'jira_get_ticket')` — substring filter matches `jira_get_ticket` exactly. OK.

2. But wait — a subtle behavior change: For a canonical tool name with an *empty* candidate list — `resolveToolAlias` returns `null` for unknown names → fall back to raw substring. OK.

3. What about the behavior of `dmtools list <canonical substring>`? E.g., `dmtools list jira` — `resolveToolAlias('jira')` → `_tools.containsKey('jira')` false, candidates empty → null → falls back to `jira` substring. Unchanged. Good.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- GitHub Issues backend for tracker-shaped `jira_*` tool calls (gh-62):
  when the ticket key matches `gh-<number>` and Jira is not configured (no
  `JIRA_BASE_PATH` / Jira auth token), `jira_get_ticket`,
  `jira_get_comments`, `jira_post_comment`, `jira_add_label`,
  `jira_remove_label`, `jira_move_to_status`, and `jira_search_by_jql`
  route to GitHub Issues on the tracker repo (`DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO`, else
  `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, else `SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) through the JS
  bridge, CLI direct dispatch, and JS-generated wrappers alike.
  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens
  the issue for Done-ish/Open-ish names; `jira_search_by_jql` supports
  key/labels/status/assignee filters — a `key` clause combined with other
  filters fetches by number and applies them client-side with JQL `in` =
  ANY semantics (absent issues skipped), keyless queries map single-value
  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an
  honest "unsupported JQL" error, since GitHub's list endpoint cannot
  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for
  anything else; search and comments walk `per_page=100` pages instead of
  silently capping at the first 100 items. Any real Jira config keeps the
  Jira path — zero regression for Java-parity environments. This unblocks
  the agents' `postPRReviewComments` `pr_approved` hand-off on `gh-N`
  tickets.
- TestRail section-aware case creation, porting Java PR
  [epam/dm.ai#462](https://github.com/epam/dm.ai/pull/462):
  `testrail_get_sections` (`project_name` + optional `suite_id`, paginated,
  always fetched fresh) and the `testrail_create_case`,
  `testrail_create_case_detailed`, `testrail_create_case_steps` tools with an
  optional `section_id` that falls back to the project's default section
  (creating a "Test Cases" section when the project has none). Markdown
  tables in text fields convert to TestRail `|||:Col|Col` format or HTML for
